newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks ease from session highs but sturdy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks ease from session highs but sturdy.

text.p: Wall Street stocks pulled back from their initial surge, taking some profits after a June employment report which showed moderate wage and job growth and sent bonds and shares soaring.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was trading up around 68 points at 7863, well below its session high of 7896. Stocks followed bonds higher after the Labor Department reported a lower-than-forecast rise in non-farm payrolls, a modest rise in hourly wages and a rise in the unemployment rate.
The long bond held to gains, up 1-5/32 to yield 6.62 percent.

"Stocks had a big rally after the employment report, then they started to pull back a bit, with the Nasdaq and the S&P index hitting new highs yesterday," Doug Myers, vice president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane. "People are getting stocks under their belt before the long weekend."
U.S. stock markets will close at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT ahead of the three-day July 4 holiday weekend. U.S. bond and foreign exchange markets will also close early, at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT.
Financial stocks were strong performers, boosted by the bond market's optimistic interest rate outlook, analysts said.

"Energy stocks have also been very active this week," Greg Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities, said. "Electrical equipment makers have been good performers and food stocks have been picking up in the past few days."
Leading the gainers on the New York Stock Exchange, Northrop Grumman Corp rose 24-1/4 to 113-1/8, after Lockheed Martin Corp said it would buy the aerospace company in a deal valued at $11.6 billion.
Analysts also said stocks sometimes made large moves going into three-day holiday weekends.
